subject.title: Bug: Telegram delivery queue recovery can replay old sendMessage replies and duplicate delivery-mirror transcript entries

question: How should OpenClaw handle shipped legacy Telegram delivery-queue rows that have a network-send `lastError` but no `recoveryState` marker?
rationale: Source inspection shows new marked rows are protected, but older shipped queue rows can lack the marker; choosing quarantine, replay, or deferred reconciliation trades possible message loss against duplicate visible delivery.

options.title: Quarantine ambiguous legacy Telegram rows
options.body: Move legacy Telegram rows with ambiguous network send errors and missing recovery markers to failed/quarantine unless reconciliation proves they were unsent.

options.title: Keep rows pending for future reconciliation
options.body: Defer these rows without replaying if maintainers want to preserve possible recovery while avoiding duplicate sends until a Telegram reconciliation surface exists.

options.title: Allow current blind replay
options.body: Accept the duplicate-delivery risk and close this issue once maintainers decide that legacy recovery should prioritize eventual delivery over duplicate prevention.

recommendation.title: Quarantine ambiguous legacy Telegram rows
recommendation.body: Move legacy Telegram rows with ambiguous network send errors and missing recovery markers to failed/quarantine unless reconciliation proves they were unsent.

likelyOwner.reason: Most connected to the queue recovery split, current replay-prevention history, and merge-time recovery policy choices.
